hyps.why: At tiny learning rates the MLP underfits within 243 epochs, so increasing the step size yields large accuracy gains.
At already large learning rates (0.08-1) Adam becomes unstable, so a further increase degrades accuracy sharply.
Reducing an excessively large learning rate restores stable training and recovers much accuracy.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, partially stabilizing training at aggressive learning rates.
With a small learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates per epoch, aggravating underfitting.
Large-batch training takes few steps and tolerates larger step sizes, so raising the learning rate helps more there.
Once L2 penalty is large (0.13-1) further increases collapse weights and cause severe underfitting, unlike negligible changes at tiny alpha.
Relaxing an over-strong L2 penalty frees the network capacity and noticeably raises accuracy.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening helps much more there than at already wide layers.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence and dead units under very large learning rates, making added depth harmful there.
